grammar_details.focus: Simple Future (will vs be going to) & Nouns

rules.usage: Predictions based on belief/opinion, instant decisions, offers, promises.
examples: I think the cheetahs will survive.
I will help the injured leopard.

rules.formula: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb
rules.usage: Plans, prior intentions, and predictions based on present evidence.
examples: Look at the dark clouds; it is going to rain.
We are going to visit Golestan National Park tomorrow.

writing_skills.topic: Types of Nouns (Common vs Proper Nouns; Singular vs Plural Nouns)
rules: A common noun names general people, places, or things (animal, forest, river).
A proper noun names a specific person, place, or day and always starts with a capital letter (Iran, Tehran, Babak, Saturday).
Regular plurals add -s or -es (cheetah -> cheetahs, box -> boxes). Irregular plurals change form (man -> men, child -> children, foot -> feet).

vocab_development.rules: Suffix -ful means 'full of' (hopeful, careful, useful, colorful, painful). Suffix -less means 'without' (hopeless, careless, useless, colorless, painless).

see_also.rules: Pronounced /s/ after voiceless sounds /p, t, k, f/ (ducks, plants). Pronounced /z/ after voiced sounds /b, d, g, v, m, n, vowels/ (pandas, plains). Pronounced /iz/ after sibilants /s, z, sh, ch, dzh/ (busses, foxes).

lessons.title: Wonders of Creation
lessons.theme: Wonders of the human body, heart, blood, universe, planets, astronomy

grammar_details.focus: Comparative & Superlative Adjectives and Adjective Order

rules.formula: Short adj + -er + than  |  more + long adj + than
rules.usage: Comparing two people, objects, or concepts.
examples: The heart is smaller than the lungs.
Telescopes are more powerful than eyeglasses.

rules.formula: the + short adj + -est  |  the most + long adj
rules.usage: Comparing one against three or more members of a group.
examples: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
The human brain is the most complex wonder of creation.

rules.formula: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material -> Noun
examples: a wonderful small round red cell

rules: Attributive adjectives sit before the noun (a healthy heart, powerful microscopes).
Predicative adjectives sit after linking verbs like be, look, feel, seem (The planet is rocky, He looks healthy).

vocab_development.rules: Two nouns combined to make a new concept. The first noun modifies the second noun (blood cell, water drop, solar system, heart beat, textbook).

see_also.rules: Stress on teen numbers is on the second syllable (fif'teen). Stress on ty numbers is on the first syllable ('fifty).

lessons.title: The Value of Knowledge
lessons.theme: Famous scientists, physicians, laboratory experiments, medicine, education

grammar_details.focus: Past Progressive Tense with when/while & Reflexive Pronouns

rules.usage: Action continuing at a specific point in the past.
examples: Dr. Gharib was examining sick children at 5 PM yesterday.

rules.formula: While + past progressive, simple past  |  Simple past + when + simple past / past progressive
examples: While he was studying medicine in France, he conducted valuable research.
The light went out when scientists were working in the laboratory.

rules.formula: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves
rules.usage: Used when the subject and object are the same person, or for emphasis.
examples: Dr. Gharib founded the hospital himself.
Children can protect themselves against microbes.

writing_skills.topic: Action Verbs vs State Verbs & Subject-Verb Agreement
rules: Action verbs describe dynamic actions (cure, invent, examine, build).
State verbs describe states, thoughts, or feelings and are rarely used in continuous tenses (know, believe, like, understand).
Singular subjects take singular verbs; plural subjects take plural verbs.

vocab_development.rules: Prefix un- means 'not' or opposite (unimportant, uneducated, unknown, uncertain). Suffixes -er and -or turn verbs into agent nouns (invent -> inventor, hunt -> hunter, farm -> farmer, act -> actor, educate -> educator).

see_also.topic: Pronunciation of Reflexive Pronouns and Sentence Stress
see_also.rules: In reflexive pronouns, the primary stress falls on 'self' or 'selves' (him'self, them'selves).

lessons.title: Traveling the World
lessons.theme: Tourism, Iranian historical cities, handicrafts, travel safety, destinations

grammar_details.focus: Modal Auxiliaries (can, may, must, should) & Prepositions

rules.formula: Subject + modal (can / may / must / should) + base verb
examples: Tourists can visit Persepolis in Fars province.
Travelers must carry their identification cards.
You should buy handicrafts to support local artists.

rules: Standard English sentence order: Subject + Verb + Object + Place + Time (S V O P T).
Example: 'Many tourists (S) visit (V) Isfahan (O) in spring (T).'

vocab_development.rules: Suffix -al converts nouns into adjectives meaning 'relating to' (culture -> cultural, history -> historical, nature -> natural, nation -> national, tradition -> traditional, religion -> religious).

see_also.topic: Rising and Falling Intonation in Requests and Statements
see_also.rules: Yes/No questions end with rising intonation (Can you help me?). Wh-questions and statements end with falling intonation (Where are you traveling?).

passages.title: Endangered Animals
passages.content: Today, there are some endangered animals on Earth. It means that we can find only a few of them alive. Some examples are pandas, tigers, and Asian elephants. Humans destroy the natural homes of the animals in the forests, lakes, and plains. When the number of people on Earth increases, they need more places for living. They cut down trees and destroy lakes. They make homes and roads instead. Then the animals won't have a place to live. They will die out. The Iranian cheetah is among these animals. This wild animal lives only in the plains of Iran. Now there are only a few Iranian cheetahs alive. If people take care of them, there is hope for this beautiful animal to live about.

passages.title: Saving Nature in Golestan National Park
passages.content: Babak and his father are visiting Golestan National Park. Babak asks Mr. Razavi the park ranger: 'Are there many cheetahs living in this forest?' Mr. Razavi replies: 'No, cheetahs live mainly in open plains. Here in Golestan we protect endangered Persian leopards and brown bears.' Babak says: 'What can students do to help?' The ranger answers: 'You should learn about wildlife, protect their natural habitats, and never throw plastic into nature.'

passages.title: A Wonder of Creation: The Human Heart
passages.content: The human body is a real wonder. It is sometimes good to think about our body and how it works. Our heart is an amazing organ. It pumps blood to all parts of our body. In fact, the heart pumps about 70 times a minute. There are millions of red and white blood cells in each drop of blood. Red blood cells carry oxygen from lungs to body cells. White blood cells defend our body against microbes. Blood also carries food nutrients. Look at the night sky. Scientists use powerful telescopes to look at the moon, stars, and distant planets. Earth is a wonderful planet in our solar system.

passages.title: Astronomy and Maragheh Observatory
passages.content: Alireza: 'Look through the telescope, Dad! I can see the rings of Saturn.' Father: 'Yes, Saturn is one of the most wonderful planets in our solar system.' Alireza: 'Did Iranian scientists study stars in ancient times?' Father: 'Certainly! Nasir al-Din al-Tusi built the famous Maragheh observatory hundreds of years ago. It had the most advanced instruments of its time.'

passages.title: Dr. Mohammad Gharib: The Dedicated Physician
passages.content: Dr. Mohammad Gharib was born in Tehran in 1288. After finishing his high school education, he went abroad to study medicine in France. In 1316, he became a distinguished physician and returned to his homeland. He founded modern pediatrics in Iran and established Children's Hospital Center in Tehran. Dr. Gharib was a dedicated doctor. He was very fond of children and examined poor children without taking any money. He wrote the first Persian textbook on children's diseases. He was not only a distinguished scientist but also a generous and kind person. He died in 1353, but people still remember his great services.

passages.title: Research at Pasteur Institute
passages.content: Sina: 'What were the researchers doing in the laboratory when we arrived?' Guide: 'They were examining microscopic cells to develop new vaccines against diseases.' Sina: 'Did Dr. Gharib also work with foreign medical centers?' Guide: 'Yes, he collaborated with world-renowned universities, but his greatest wish was to train dedicated Iranian doctors to cure sick children in our own country.'

passages.title: Iran: A Wonderful Destination
passages.content: Every year, millions of people travel to different parts of the world. Tourism is very important for many countries. Iran is an ancient country with a rich culture and thousands of historical attractions. Cities like Shiraz, Isfahan, Yazd, and Mashhad attract many domestic and international tourists each year. Tourists visit ancient monuments like Persepolis and Pasargadae. They enjoy beautiful gardens, mosques, and traditional bazaars. Iranian people are known worldwide for being warm, kind, and hospitable. In every city, tourists can find delicious traditional meals and colorful handicrafts like carpets, pottery, and tilework to take home as souvenirs.

passages.title: Planning a Trip to Isfahan
passages.content: Diego: 'Excuse me, can you help me choose the best historical attractions in Isfahan?' Travel Agent: 'Certainly! You should definitely visit Naqsh-e Jahan Square, Si-o-se-pol, and Chehel Sotoun palace.' Diego: 'Are there good places to buy traditional souvenirs?' Travel Agent: 'Yes, around the grand bazaar you can find skilled craftspeople making miniature paintings, pottery, and exquisite handwoven Persian rugs.'
